headline: Binary-search the change from rising to falling
statement: Given a mountain array arr that strictly increases to one interior peak then strictly decreases, return the peak index in logarithmic time.
constraints: A strict mountain shape with an interior peak is guaranteed
intuition: A mountain rises before its peak and falls after it. Compare the middle value with the next value to learn which side you are on. A rising comparison keeps the right side; a falling comparison keeps the middle and left side. Repeat until one index remains.
approach: Maintain inclusive bounds containing the peak.
When arr[mid] < arr[mid+1], set left to mid+1.
Otherwise set right to mid; stop when bounds meet.
correctness: A mountain rises only before its unique peak and falls from its peak onward. Each slope comparison selects an interval that still contains the peak. The interval shrinks strictly, and its sole remaining index must be the peak.
bruteForce: Scan to find the maximum value, costing O(n) time.

complexity.explanation: The interval roughly halves each round and uses only indices.

pitfalls: The input guarantee is essential; arbitrary arrays may have multiple peaks.
Use right=mid on a falling edge because mid may be the peak.
With left<right, mid+1 is always in bounds.
